hints: Because the pulleys are smooth and the hanging particles are in equilibrium, the string tensions are equal to the weights $A\text{ N}$ and $B\text{ N}$.

Notice carefully that the angles $30^\circ$ and $40^\circ$ are given with the vertical: the horizontal components are $A\sin 30^\circ$ and $B\sin 40^\circ$, and vertical components are $A\cos 30^\circ$ and $B\cos 40^\circ$.
Set up the horizontal equilibrium equation $A\sin 30^\circ = B\sin 40^\circ$ and express $A$ in terms of $B$ as $A = B\frac{\sin 40^\circ}{\sin 30^\circ} = 2B\sin 40^\circ$.
Substitute into the vertical equation $A\cos 30^\circ + B\cos 40^\circ = 25$ and solve for $B$, then calculate $A$ to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces horizontally at the central $25\text{ N}$ particle in equilibrium, noting that angles are given to the vertical:
$$A\sin 30^\circ = B\sin 40^\circ \implies A = B \frac{\sin 40^\circ}{\sin 30^\circ} = B \frac{\sin 40^\circ}{0.5} = 2B\sin 40^\circ$$

Resolve forces vertically, equating the upward vertical components of tension to the downward weight of $25\text{ N}$:
$$A\cos 30^\circ + B\cos 40^\circ = 25$$

Substitute $A = 2B\sin 40^\circ$ into the vertical equilibrium equation and factor out $B$:
$$(2B\sin 40^\circ)\cos 30^\circ + B\cos 40^\circ = 25 \implies B(2\sin 40^\circ \cos 30^\circ + \cos 40^\circ) = 25$$

Compute the bracketed coefficient and solve for $B$:
$$2\sin 40^\circ \cos 30^\circ + \cos 40^\circ \approx 2(0.642788)(0.866025) + 0.766044 = 1.113344 + 0.766044 = 1.879388$$
$$B = \frac{25}{1.879388} \approx 13.3022 \approx 13.3$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the condition for a particle in coplanar equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_x = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad \Sigma F_y = 0$$
Since the pulleys are smooth and the hanging weights are in vertical equilibrium, the tension in the left string equals $A\text{ N}$ and the tension in the right string equals $B\text{ N}$.

Observe that the angles $30^\circ$ and $40^\circ$ are measured from the vertical. Set up the horizontal equilibrium equation (taking right as positive):
$$B\sin 40^\circ - A\sin 30^\circ = 0 \implies A\sin 30^\circ = B\sin 40^\circ$$

Rearrange to express $A$ in terms of $B$ by dividing both sides by $\sin 30^\circ = 0.5$:
$$A = \frac{B\sin 40^\circ}{0.5} = 2B\sin 40^\circ \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

Set up the vertical equilibrium equation (taking upwards as positive), balancing upward components against the central $25\text{ N}$ weight:
$$A\cos 30^\circ + B\cos 40^\circ = 25 \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Factor out $B$ on the left-hand side:
$$B\left(2\sin 40^\circ \cos 30^\circ + \cos 40^\circ\right) = 25$$

Substitute the unrounded value of $B$ into Equation 1 to find $A$:
$$A = 2 \times 13.3022 \times 0.642788 \approx 17.1010 = 17.1 \text{ (to 3 s.f.)}$$

ai_rubric.Applying Coplanar Equilibrium: Resolves horizontally ($A\sin 30^\circ = B\sin 40^\circ$) and vertically ($A\cos 30^\circ + B\cos 40^\circ = 25$), solving simultaneously to find $A = 17.1$ and $B = 13.3$.
